thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging @Priya (oncall) — GPU pool 'preemptible-west-2' dropping below target. Queue growth detected, throttling observed. See alert: https://redwood.incidents/1776601234
Priya: Ack, I'm on it. Pulling metrics now.
Priya: TL;DR — queue length for generation requests jumped to ~4200, 95% tail latency > 4s, errors = 429 throttles + connection resets.
Mike: I see a correlated spike in preemptible evictions around 1776601000-1776601200 (mass reclaim events from cloud). Autoscaler tried to spin up fallback nodes but hit max_nodes cap.
Alex: Autoscaler logs show repeated failures: 
```
W 2026-03-14T15:20:34 autoscaler: request nodes=50 -> failed: quotaExceeded
E 2026-03-14T15:21:01 autoscaler: reached max_nodes (60) for pool=reserved-gpu
```
Mike: Cloud also returned "INSUFFICIENT_HOST_CAPACITY" for several launch attempts. Spot availability in region is unstable right now.
Taylor: Support: three customers reported degraded generation throughput; a fourth saw timeouts. I'm triaging SLAs, customers impacted: acme-ai, boutique-saas, searchly. Sending status to accounts.
Jess: Are we failing over to CPU fallback or smaller models? What's the immediate mitigation?
Priya: Quick mitigations I'm doing now: 1) pause low-priority batch jobs (jobqueue:low); 2) enable emergency_burst on dedicated pool (if capacity available); 3) apply temporary rate limit increase for paid-enterprise customers only. Executing step 1 now.
Priya: Command: `./runbooks/infra pause-low-priority.sh --queue jobqueue:low` (kickoff).
Deploy Bot: Started jobpause workflow (runid=rb-9f3).
Priya: Paused ~120 low-priority jobs, reclaimed ~8 GPUs. Queue reduced by ~300 in the first 2 mins.
Mike: I'm attempting to increase reserved-gpu max_nodes from 60 -> 90. Running change, but cloud quota checks might block. Command: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling ... --max-num-replicas=90`
Alex: If quota increase fails, alternative is to route traffic to model-quantized variants (smaller instance footprint). Can someone enable model fallbacks for the next 30 min?
Priya: Flipping model-fallback policy to prefer quantized-1.2x for non-enterprise customers. Patch applied.
Taylor: Noted — I'm communicating to the three impacted customers that we're mitigating and providing ETA ~20-40m.
Mike: Autoscaler change status: cloud returned error "QUOTA_LIMITS_EXCEEDED" for GPUs. I filed a fast-path ticket with cloud support. Meanwhile we can: a) drain cache-heavy nodes to free reserved GPUs, b) attempt cross-region failover to preemptible-east1 if acceptable latency.
Alex: Cross-region has data residency implications for some enterprise customers. Jess/PMs please flag if any impacted.
Jess: I will check list. acme-ai is fine with cross-region. boutique-saas on contract says no cross-region. We need to prioritize reserved capacity for them.
Priya: Handoff note: My shift ends in ~18m. If we still have active mitigation, I'll hand off to Alex. Alex, please prepare to take oncall if autoscaler still failing.
Alex: Ready. I'll pick up if still open. Next steps I'm doing now: 1) collect all failing trace ids and make temporary blocklist for retry storms; 2) increase low-rate token bucket for enterprise customers; 3) coordinate with infra for cross-region placement.
Priya: Observability checklist: dashboards -> token-consumption, queue-length, autoscaler-events, spot-evictions. Saved a snapshot to the incident timeline.
Incident Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-9 — "preemptible fallback exhaustion". Current severity: sev2.
PagerDuty: Pager escalated to oncall->secondary due to ongoing customer impact.
Mike: Update: cloud support opened case CS-8812, gave provisional capacity in east1 (spot) but ETA is 35m. We can initiate cross-region failover now and shift a portion of traffic (10-20%) to east1 to reduce pressure.
Taylor: I'm drafting an interim status update for customers with relevant guidance (model fallbacks on, expect increased latency for non-enterprise).
Priya: Let's not do a full traffic split without product approval. We'll do a controlled 10% shift for public customers. Jess, ok?
Jess: Ok for public customers. boutique-saas and acme-ai excluded.
Alex: Executing controlled 10% split: `dispatchctl route set --from pool=preemptible-west-2 --to=preemptible-east-1 --percent=10`
Deploy Bot: Routing update applied (op:route-cc2).
Priya: After 15m, queue dropped from 4200 -> 2100. Throttles decreased ~60%. Good signal.
Taylor: Support: boutique-saas reported continued latency; offering priority bump to reserved pool until we restore capacity. They accepted temporary reserved allocation for their production traffic.
Mike: Reserved pool still near max but we freed ~12 GPUs by draining non-critical stateful tasks.
Alex: Planning follow-ups: - postmortem to detail autoscaler thresholds & quota handling - add playbook step to immediate cross-region failover when preemptible evictions > N% - run a stress test of reserved-burst path monthly - revisit reserved capacity SLAs for enterprise customers
Priya: Handoff to Alex now. All active mitigations handed over. I am going offline for shift change.
Alex: Taking over. I'll keep the thread updated and create the postmortem draft after stabilization. Assigning action items: Mike (infra) - cloud quota follow-up and increase baseline reserved nodes; Jess (product) - contract & cross-region policy review; Taylor (support) - customer comms & SLA notes; Priya - add incident notes and telemetry links.
Alex: Current status at 1776603380 — queue ~1400, throttles reducing, autoscaler pending cloud quota resolution. Marking incident as "mitigated (partial)". Will update when fully resolved. :white_check_mark:
